verificationNote: NIST entries verified against NIST IR 8547 ipd (November 2024) Tables 2-7 and the NIST PQC project page. CNSA 2.0 entries remain needs-check — nsa.gov and media.defense.gov return HTTP 403 to automated fetches and must be checked by hand. See README.md.

IR8547.title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
IR8547.status: INITIAL PUBLIC DRAFT — comment period closed 2025-01-10, not yet final as of 2026-08-01

criticalCaveat: NIST IR 8547 is an INITIAL PUBLIC DRAFT. Its dates are NIST's stated intent, not binding final guidance. Any customer-facing use MUST say 'draft guidance' — presenting draft dates as final is the exact error that loses a technically literate buyer.

definitions.deprecated: The algorithm and key length/strength may be used, but there is some security risk. The data owner must examine this risk potential and decide whether to continue use. [IR8547 §4, quoting SP 800-131A]
definitions.disallowed: The algorithm, key length/strength, parameter set, or scheme is no longer allowed for the stated purpose. [IR8547 §4]
definitions.legacyUse: May only be used to process already-protected information (e.g. decrypt existing ciphertext, verify an existing signature). [IR8547 §4]

replacements.note: Only approved post-quantum key-establishment scheme at present [IR8547 §4.1.2]. Hybrid (classical + ML-KEM) is a common transitional deployment.

deadlines.note: IMPORTANT: larger RSA keys do NOT buy extra time. RSA-3072 and above are disallowed after 2035 on the same schedule.

algorithms.explanation: RSA security rests on integer factorisation, which Shor's algorithm solves in polynomial time on a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer.

replacements.note: Conservative hash-based alternative; larger signatures. Preferred where signature size is not constrained and long validity is required.

deadlines.note: P-256 and above are all disallowed after 2035. Curve size does not extend the deadline.

algorithms.explanation: ECDSA rests on the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem, broken by Shor's algorithm.
EdDSA is elliptic-curve based and broken by Shor's algorithm. Listed explicitly in IR 8547 Table 2 — the current scanner does not detect it, which is a coverage gap worth closing.

deadlines.source: IR8547 Table 4 (Finite Field DH and MQV; Elliptic Curve DH and MQV)

algorithms.explanation: Diffie-Hellman key agreement is broken by Shor's algorithm. This is the primary harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure: recorded sessions can be decrypted retroactively once the key exchange is broken.
algorithms.hndlSourceQuote: IR8547 §4.1.2: 'in order to mitigate the risk of "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks on network communications, application-specific guidance ... may require or recommend migration to quantum-resistant key establishment schemes before the classical schemes are generally disallowed.' — i.e. the 2035 date is a ceiling, not a target, for anything carrying long-lived secrets.

algorithms.verificationNote: DSA does NOT appear as a separate row in IR 8547 Table 2 (which lists ECDSA, EdDSA, RSA). DSA was already withdrawn for signature generation in earlier FIPS 186 revisions. Confirm the correct citation before making deadline claims about DSA specifically — do not reuse the RSA/ECDSA dates by assumption.
algorithms.explanation: DSA rests on the discrete logarithm problem and is broken by Shor's algorithm. Already discouraged for new use independently of quantum concerns.
MD5 is classically broken by collision attacks. Not a quantum issue — already unfit for security use.
algorithms.reportingNote: MUST NOT count toward the post-quantum risk score. Classical hygiene finding — track in a separate panel so PQC metrics are not inflated.

algorithms.quantumAttack: Grover (quadratic preimage speedup, not a break)
algorithms.explanation: IR 8547 Table 7 lists SHA-1 at 80 bits collision security (security category <1) and 160 bits preimage security (category 1). Classically deprecated due to collision attacks; the quantum impact on hashes is a parameter concern, not a break.
algorithms.reportingNote: Classical hygiene finding. Track separately from PQC risk.

algorithms.explanation: ECB mode leaks plaintext structure — identical blocks produce identical ciphertext. A mode-of-operation flaw, unrelated to quantum computing.
algorithms.reportingNote: Classical hygiene finding. Track separately from PQC risk.

algorithms.explanation: IR 8547 §4.1.3: NIST's symmetric standards are 'significantly less vulnerable to known quantum attacks than the public-key cryptography standards', and all approved symmetric primitives providing at least 128 bits of classical security are believed to meet at least Category 1. Table 6: AES-128 = 128 bits / Category 1, AES-192 = 192 bits / Category 3, AES-256 = 256 bits / Category 5.
algorithms.reportingNote: DO NOT flag AES-128 as quantum-critical. NIST places it at security Category 1, i.e. adequate. Flagging it inflates the risk score and a knowledgeable buyer will notice. Note separately that CNSA 2.0 requires AES-256 for US national security systems — that is an NSS-specific requirement, not a general NIST one.
algorithms.symmetricNote: NIST has a few symmetric standards at the 112-bit security level (e.g. three-key TDEA) which IR 8547 §4.1.3 says will be disallowed in 2030.

pqcAlgorithms.note: IR 8547 §4.1.2: ML-KEM is the ONLY approved post-quantum key-establishment scheme at present.
pqcAlgorithms.sourceErratum: IR 8547 ipd Table 5 mislabels the 192- and 256-bit rows as 'ML-DSA-768' and 'ML-DSA-1024'. These are typographical errors in the draft; the correct names are ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024.

pqcAlgorithms.note: Stateless hash-based. Conservative security assumptions, large signatures. Suited to firmware/code signing with long validity.
Stateful hash-based signatures. IR 8547 Table 3 lists these as post-quantum signature options at 192 and 256 bits. Stateful — key management is unforgiving; suited to firmware signing.
Stateful hash-based signatures, listed in IR 8547 Table 3 at 192 and 256 bits.

pqcAlgorithms.status: NOT YET PUBLISHED — selected for ongoing standardization, process underway
pqcAlgorithms.warning: DO NOT cite 'FIPS 206' as an existing standard. As of 2026-08-01 the NIST PQC project page describes Falcon as selected for ongoing standardization with the process underway; no published FIPS number was confirmed. Verify before any customer-facing reference.

pqcAlgorithms.status: Selected in the 4th round; standardization underway, not yet published
pqcAlgorithms.note: Backup KEM with different mathematical assumptions to ML-KEM. IR 8547 §4.1.2 notes NIST expects to select one or more alternatives to ML-KEM in future.

citation.document: NIST PQC project page; IR 8547 ipd §4.1.2
